I need to output JSON only, covering three steps, with titles under 80 characters and explanations under 300. The third step is supporting, so it stays as its own item. For the first step, the endpoint returns a plain-text receipt of the user's own order and gives a 404 otherwise. I'll check that the order lookup is scoped to the user, and that the route sits after the auth middleware. I still need to note how the 404 case is handled.

Next I'm looking at step two, the receipt renderer, which builds the text from the items and total and caches results per order id in memory for an hour with no eviction. I want to confirm the cache key is fine given the lookup is already scoped to the user, and check whether a cancelled order could be served stale within that hour. For step three, the config bumps the rate limit from 60 to 600 and adds receipt settings that the shown code never reads.

{"answer":{"pass":"tour","tour":{"steps":[{"stepId":"s1","title":"Signed-in users download a plain-text receipt for their own order","explanation":"Returns the receipt as text/plain for an order the user owns, or 404 otherwise. Check that findOrder scopes by req.user.id and that the route sits behind requireUser."},{"stepId":"s2","title":"Receipt text lists items and total, cached in memory for an hour","explanation":"Builds the receipt from order items and sums quantity times price. Results are cached per order id for a hard-coded hour with no eviction, and the cache is not cleared when an order changes, such as on cancel. Check both."},{"stepId":"s3","title":"Config adds receipt settings and raises the rate limit tenfold","explanation":"Raises rateLimit.perMinute from 60 to 600, which the request did not ask for. Adds cache.ttlSeconds.receipts and receipts.currency/footer, but no code reads them, so the TTL is still hard-coded."}],"merges":[]}}}

The tour is already built: <tour_skeleton> lists its steps in reading order. A "flow" step starts at an entry point (an HTTP route, a page, a command), listed under entries, and reads the changed code that entry runs, callers before callees. "passes through" names code an earlier step already read. A "supporting" step holds changes no flow runs: an API schema, docs, tests, or other changes by area. Each step has the code's own title, which names the code ("PUT /api/items/{id}", a function name, "Tests"), and the code's explanation. A hunk ID with lines is the part of that hunk on those lines; a hunk ID alone is the whole hunk.

The steps and the code in them are fixed. Write, for every step, by its id:
- title: what the step does, as behavior a user or caller would notice, in plain language, at most 80 characters ("Save a host's token", not "PUT /api/account-connections/{domain}/token" or a function name). Don't repeat the code's title: the reviewer sees it under yours.
- explanation: one or two sentences, at most 300 characters, on what this step changes and what the reviewer should check in it.

merges: you may merge a supporting step into the step it belongs with, such as docs into the flow they document, or tests into the flow they test. Each merge names the supporting step (stepId), the step it joins (intoStepId) and a one-sentence reason. Merge only supporting steps, never a flow, each at most once, and never into a step you merge elsewhere. A supporting step that belongs with several steps or none stays. Most tours need no merges.
